items.one_liner: ReplayRCA evaluates LLM agent failure diagnosis via counterfactual replay, revealing that strong post-hoc diagnosers do not necessarily make effective live supervisors.
items.summary: Researchers introduced ReplayRCA, a counterfactual replay benchmark that measures post-hoc diagnosis and live oversight of multi-step agent failures by restoring the environment to the state preceding a failed step and testing whether a corrective action restores task success. Evaluating 13 frontier models on OpsWorld tasks, the best model achieved a causal repair score of +51.3 points, with performance varying significantly between post-hoc analysis and live supervision. Notably, a small open-source model (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash) tied for the best live supervisor, while a top post-hoc diagnoser (GPT-6.1 Sol) performed poorly in live oversight, proving that offline diagnostic capability is a weak proxy for live intervention performance.
items.bottom_line: Counterfactual replay evaluation shows that post-hoc diagnostic performance for LLM agents is a poor predictor of live supervision effectiveness.

items.title: LEAP: Efficient LLM Inference Scheduling with Generalizable Length Prediction
items.one_liner: LEAP is an efficient, adaptive length prediction system that reduces LLM serving latency through asynchronous CPU execution.
items.summary: Length-aware scheduling improves request latency in LLM serving by prioritizing shorter requests, but length predictors often suffer accuracy drops under domain shifts and incur heavy computational overhead. To address this, researchers introduced LEAP, an efficient length prediction system featuring fast online adaptation and asynchronous CPU execution. LEAP reuses the serving model's prefill hidden states via a linear readout and updates parameters at test time using recursive least squares without gradient computations. Serving experiments demonstrated that LEAP reduces average per-token latency by up to 40.8% while achieving higher throughput with significantly fewer parameters than baseline models.
key_facts: Parameter Reduction: 30,569× fewer predictor parameters than baseline
items.bottom_line: Reusing prefill hidden states for online length prediction enables fast scheduling optimization and lowers LLM serving latency without costly retraining.

items.title: Capability-Grounded Agentic Planning
items.one_liner: Capability-Grounded Agentic Planning pairs classical PDDL planners with LLMs to eliminate trial-and-error failures in tool use.
items.summary: Standard LLM agents often rely on trial-and-error tool calling with no execution guarantees. Capability-Grounded Agentic Planning (CGAP) addresses this by compiling tool catalogs deterministically into PDDL models, turning natural-language requests into goals via an LLM, and solving the model with a classical planner. Because tool outputs are dynamic, the model uses abstract tracking, letting an LLM add entity-specific calls during execution while verifiers check results against the request. Across multiple benchmarks like ToolSandbox and ComplexFuncBench, CGAP outperforms standard tool-calling agents by up to 28.9 points.
key_facts: Benchmarks: ToolSandbox, ComplexFuncBench, BFCL multi-turn, tau^2-bench retail
items.bottom_line: CGAP combines deterministic PDDL compilation with LLM verification to boost tool-calling agent performance by up to 28.9 points.
